harnesses.notes: CONFIRMED this review (direct fetch of the settings-reference index + detail entries, code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference): 9 more keys with a clear restrictive direction, not previously in mergeRules — disableDesktopLocalSessions ('Turn off Desktop Code sessions that run on the device, leaving SSH to other hosts and cloud', Managed-only, lock -> anyTrue), gatewayInternalNetworks ('Let /login reach a cloud gateway on public IPv4 space your organization uses internally', Managed-only, grant exception list -> union), skipWebFetchPreflight ('Skip the WebFetch hostname check when Anthropic is unreachable'; true loosens the check, so restrictive-wins is anyFalse), desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays ('Set an age limit in days for Claude Desktop and Cowork transcripts', retention limit alongside the existing cleanupPeriodDays -> min), availableModelsMatch (string enum 'prefix' (default, looser) / 'exact', 'Choose how availableModels entries match model IDs', Managed-only -> strictest, order [exact, prefix]), enforceAvailableModels (bool default false, 'Keep the /model Default choice inside your availableModels allowlist'; page confirms that once any managed source sets it, non-managed files are ignored for this key -> anyTrue), disableWorkflows ('Turn dynamic workflows off for everyone; use enableWorkflows for yourself' — same disableX-is-restrictive shape as disableRemoteControl etc. above -> anyTrue), disableAgentView ('Turn off background agents and agent view' -> anyTrue), forceLoginOrgUUID ('Pin claude.ai logins to your organization; only a managed source enforces it' — restriction allowlist, same key/shape confirmed on Claude Desktop's enterprise-configuration article -> intersect). Reviewed and deliberately left out of mergeRules: forceLoginMethod ('Restrict login to claude.ai, Claude Console, or a cloud gateway' — an enum with no defined cross-method strictness order), autoUpdatesChannel and minimumVersion (auto-update convenience settings, not managed-exclusive, and not clearly security-restrictive in either direction). Mimir writes the file-based managed tier. An MDM profile for com.anthropic.claudecode ranks above the file and, with the default managedSourcesBehavior 'first-wins', hides Mimir's file completely. Deploy settings for Claude Code through Mimir only. Since v2.1.242, setting managedSourcesBehavior to 'merge' in the highest-ranked source (the MDM profile) makes Claude Code compose every admin source instead of hiding lower ones — an org that wants both an MDM profile and Mimir's file applied must opt in there, not in Mimir's file. Claude Code also reads a managed-settings.d/*.json drop-in directory alongside managed-settings.json; Mimir does not write into that directory yet. CONFIRMED (raw fetch): drop-in files merge alphabetically after managed-settings.json — plain scalars last-file-wins, lists union+dedupe, nested blocks merge key-by-key, but fallbackModel, managedMcpServers, extraKnownMarketplaces and modelPicker are replaced whole by the later file rather than merged. Also confirmed: the allowedProviders cross-source merge now requires Claude Code >= v2.1.285 to take effect. CONFIRMED this review (raw fetch of settings-reference's index table): 7 previously-unconfirmed keys now have pinned-down descriptions — allowedChannelPlugins ('Replace the default allowlist of channel plugins that can push messages', restriction allowlist -> intersect), channelsEnabled ('Allow channels for your organization', kill switch -> anyFalse), disableCommandPluginSources ('Block plugins that install by running a marketplace-declared command', lock -> anyTrue), forceRemoteSettingsRefresh ('Block startup until server-managed settings are freshly fetched', lock -> anyTrue), crossSessionInbound ('Choose whether Claude Code delivers messages from your other sessions, shows a notice without delivering them, or refuses them', enum -> strictest, order [refuse, hold, accept]), enableArtifact ('Turn the Artifact tool off with a false in any file; no file can turn it back on', kill switch -> anyFalse), disableRemoteControl ('Turn off Remote Control everywhere it can start', lock -> anyTrue). policyHelper and parentSettingsBehavior remain excluded from mergeRules — both are delivery/opt-in controls (which executable computes policy; whether a host app's settings merge in) rather than a restriction value with a clear more-/less-restrictive direction for Mimir's own fragment-merge purposes.

outputs.description: Managed settings (highest file-based precedence; users cannot override).

harnesses.notes: Claude Desktop only reads the com.anthropic.claudefordesktop managed-preferences domain; there is no file-based alternative. Mimir writes that plist in /Library/Managed Preferences directly, which Apple does not document for third parties: macOS may remove it when profiles change, and Mimir restores it within seconds. Do not also deploy a vendor profile for this domain. Claude Desktop reads policy at launch; users must restart the app. CONFIRMED via direct raw fetches of https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration: the plist is documented as read PER-USER, literally '/Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.plist', not the single device-wide path Mimir currently writes and this entry's output models — Mimir needs to write (or additionally write) the per-user path before this policy is reliably read; see PR 'Needs Mimir change'. builtinBrowserAllowedDomains, sshHostAllowlist and coworkEgressAllowedHosts are string[] restriction allowlists; blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories and disableBypassPermissionsMode are boolean kill switches; disabledBuiltinTools is a string[] deny list; builtinToolPolicy is a per-tool allow/ask/blocked map. organizationInstructions (free-text model guidance) and inferenceModels (wholesale model-list override) remain excluded as not policy-relevant. requireCoworkFullVmSandbox is still marked Deprecated in the vendor table with no replacement key confirmed yet — kept here since deprecated keys typically still function during a migration window; recheck next review. Disable to keep tool approvals per-call or session-scoped only' -> anyFalse), disableEssentialTelemetry (bool, default false, added 1.2581.0, crash/performance reports -> anyTrue), disableNonessentialTelemetry (bool, default false, added 1.2581.0, product-usage analytics/diagnostic uploads -> anyTrue), disableNonessentialServices (bool, default false, added 1.2581.0, blocks connector-favicon/artifact-preview/MCP-Apps-widget/spellcheck egress -> anyTrue), developerModeEnabled (bool, added 2.37337.1, 'Let users turn on Developer Mode. When off, the app's developer tools... are unavailable' -> anyFalse), scheduledTasksEnabled (bool, added 2.110.0, 'Allow scheduled tasks in Cowork and Code. When off, the Scheduled page is hidden' -> anyFalse), builtinBrowserEnabled (bool, default false, added 2.2553.0, gates the in-app browser -> anyFalse), builtinBrowserBlockedDomains (string[] deny list, added 2.2553.0, denies builtinBrowserAllowedDomains -> union), allowedPluginMcpServers (object[] restriction allowlist, added 2.2553.0, 'Servers plugins may connect in sessions...an empty list allows none' -> intersect), deniedPluginMcpServers (object[] deny list keyed on serverUrl, added 2.16120.0, 'even if the allowed list admits them' -> union, denies allowedPluginMcpServers). egressProxyUrl/egressProxyPacUrl are MDM-only plain string config values with no restriction/grant direction — no mergeRule added. userPluginMarketplacesEnabled, userPluginUploadsEnabled, disableDeploymentModeChooser and disableDeepLinkRegistration appear in the vendor table but weren't pinned down with a full quote this pass — left for a follow-up (see PR 'Unverified'). RESOLVED this review (direct fetch of claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/configuration, the third-party/MDM-deployment reference page, i.e. exactly Mimir's own deployment method): all 4 of those keys now have a full quote, plus a definitive answer on requireCoworkFullVmSandbox. userPluginMarketplacesEnabled (bool, since 1.37937.0, 'Allow users to add plugin marketplaces. When off, marketplaces your organization did not provision are hidden...' -> anyFalse); userPluginUploadsEnabled (bool, since 1.37937.0, 'Allow users to add their own plugins. When off, every in-app option for adding one is hidden...' -> anyFalse); disableDeploymentModeChooser (bool, default false, since 1.3834.0, 'Users see only this provider at the login screen. The option to sign in to Claude.ai is hidden.' -> anyTrue); disableDeepLinkRegistration (bool, default false, since 1.6889.0, 'Stop external apps and websites from opening Claude Desktop via claude:// links.' -> anyTrue). Remove it from your configuration.' Mimir writes exactly this kind of third-party/MDM deployment, so this key's mergeRule is removed below as dead policy. Also found (same fetch): managedMcpServers entries can carry a per-server toolPolicy ('blocked'/'ask'/'allow', wildcard keys like 'read_*', strictest match wins) — not modeled as a mergeRule yet since it's a nested per-entry field rather than a flat key path; flagged for a future review. Separately, the catalog's own managedMcpServers path had no mergeRule at all despite being a declared jsonEncodedKey — since it is a grant list of org-provided MCP servers (same family as Claude Code's own managedMcpServers, which is union), added a union rule below so multiple admin fragments compose instead of one replacing another. harnesses.notes: Mimir writes the system managed config, which overrides global, project and remote (.well-known/opencode) config. An MDM profile for ai.opencode.managed also overrides everything and conflicts with Mimir's output. Full precedence (lowest to highest), confirmed against the opencode source: remote (.well-known/opencode) < global < OPENCODE_CONFIG < project < .opencode/ dirs < OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT < Mimir's managed file dir < the ai.opencode.managed mobileconfig. opencode has no per-MCP-server allow/deny list; governance is only via remote-provided servers with a per-server enabled toggle (re-checked this review; still true — opencode.ai itself remained unreachable for a direct fetch, blocked by this session's network policy, but WebSearch snippets of the official docs.opencode.ai/docs/policies/ page, consistent across many locale mirrors of opencode.ai, found nothing about MCP). The 'strictest' ordering used below for share/permission.* is Mimir's own more-restrictive-wins policy choice, not a vendor-documented cross-source merge rule — opencode's own docs only describe plain tier override. NEW this review (WebSearch-quoted from the official policies doc, not direct-fetch-confirmed): opencode now documents `experimental.policies` as the forward-looking replacement for disabled_providers/enabled_providers, confirming the existing union mergeRule below is the right shape — policies are {effect, action: 'provider.use', resource} statements, last-matching-statement-wins, global config's policies take priority over project config's on the same provider, and an unmatched provider defaults to allowed. The docs give a migration path (deny-per-provider for disabled_providers; deny-all-then-allow-selected for enabled_providers) but no removal date for the older keys, so disabled_providers/enabled_providers are left as-is below.

outputs.description: Managed opencode.json (keys: mcp, permission, provider, model, disabled_providers, enabled_providers, share, autoupdate, …).

harnesses.notes: requirements.toml holds hard constraints users cannot change (deployed locally or via an MDM profile for com.openai.codex using the requirements_toml_base64 key); managed_config.toml holds managed defaults the user can still override at runtime (MDM key config_toml_base64). Precedence is requirements.toml > cloud-managed configuration defaults (ChatGPT Business/Enterprise) > managed_config.toml. CORRECTED this review (confirmed against the codex-rs source): allowed_sandbox_modes is NOT deprecated, it is still a live, actively-tested requirements.toml field alongside allowed_permission_profiles, where any profile omitted from the list (including future built-ins) is denied. managed_config.toml itself is the one being phased out — Codex's own source calls it a 'best effort' legacy layer being replaced by requirements.toml, and it is already fully removed on Windows. Codex's own internal cross-source composition for the allowed_* fields is actually last-layer-wins override, not intersect; the 'intersect' strategy below is a deliberate Mimir-side policy choice (stricter than Codex's native default) layered on top of that, not a mirror of vendor behavior. CORRECTED this review (confirmed via a direct fetch of github.com/openai/codex/issues/39973): approval_policy = 'untrusted' was retired in Codex CLI 0.149.0 (PR #39630, merged 2026-08-20) — the CLI now refuses to start with that value present ('approval_policy = "untrusted" is no longer supported; remove this setting'), with no direct equivalent (the issue notes 'on-request' is weaker and per-project trust_level='untrusted' isn't equivalent either). Removed 'untrusted' from the managed_config.toml strictest order below accordingly. A separate, lower-confidence lead (blog-sourced only, not confirmed against an official changelog or PR) claims 'on-failure' was also removed earlier (0.143 alpha) — this review found a merged, primary-source PR (github.com/openai/codex/pull/11631, 'chore(core): Deprecate approval_policy: on-failure', merged 2026-02-12) confirming on-failure is DEPRECATED, but OpenAI's own localized config-reference mirrors (developers.openai.com/es-419 etc., WebSearch-quoted, developers.openai.com itself still unreachable for direct fetch) as of Oct 2026 still list it as a valid-but-deprecated value, contradicting the 'fully removed in 0.143-alpha' claim. Kept 'on-failure' in the strictest order below since no removal is confirmed — only deprecation; see PR 'Unverified'.

outputs.description: Legacy/deprecated managed defaults layered above the user's config.toml (approval_policy, sandbox_mode, otel telemetry block, check_for_update_on_startup, …); OpenAI is phasing this file out in favor of requirements.toml and has already removed it on Windows.

harnesses.notes: MAJOR CHANGE this review, CONFIRMED via a direct fetch of the official google-gemini/gemini-cli README: the README now carries a top-of-page notice, verbatim, 'Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18th, 2026,' linking to Google's own blog post (added to documentation above), plus a second notice that Gemini CLI 'has not been optimized for Gemini 4 Argon' and to use Antigravity for that model. The README states this replacement applies to 'Unpaid tier and Google One users'; it does not mention enterprise/Code Assist Standard or Enterprise tiers one way or the other, so whether paid/enterprise users (the audience Mimir's managed-config mechanism targets) retain full support is NOT confirmed from an official source — secondary press coverage (not applied here) claims enterprise users keep access, but developers.googleblog.com itself was unreachable for a direct fetch this review (blocked by this session's network policy) to verify that detail. Given this, HOLD on recommending 'supported' promotion until enterprise-tier continuity and Antigravity's own admin/MDM story are confirmed from an official source — this reverses last review's 'Recommend promoting to supported.' The device-level mechanism described below was CONFIRMED device-level as of the 2026-10-05 review and is presumably still accurate for whichever Gemini CLI install remains supported, but has not been re-verified this pass given the bigger open question above. Casing confirmed exact: system overrides at /Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/settings.json, defaults at system-defaults.json in the same folder (env override: GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH). Precedence System overrides > Workspace > User > System defaults (arrays/objects merge rather than replace). Keys: tools.core (array, tool/command allowlist -> union), tools.sandbox (string enforce e.g. 'docker'), mcp.allowed (confirmed true allow-list, intersect: 'a server must be permitted by every source to run') + mcpServers (canonical server defs, union-by-name, System > Workspace > User on name collisions), telemetry.enabled / telemetry.logPrompts (bool kill switches -> anyFalse), privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled (bool -> anyFalse), security.disableYoloMode (bool lock -> anyTrue), security.auth.enforcedType (string, last/admin wins). excludeTools/tools.exclude is now deprecated in favor of policy-engine deny rules. The TOML policy engine ([[rule]] with toolName/decision/priority, plus richer fields subagent/mcpName/toolAnnotations/commandRegex/modes/denyMessage) loaded from Admin dirs (/Library/Application Support/GeminiCli/policies on macOS) uses a 5-tier priority system (Default=1, Extension=2, Workspace=3 [currently non-functional, see gemini-cli#18186 — confirmed this review via a direct fetch of that issue to still be open as of 2026-10-13, and now confirmed, via its cross-reference to gemini-cli#21580, to be an INTENTIONAL, TEMPORARY maintainer disablement rather than an accidental bug; also newly confirmed this review: final rule priority = tier_base + (toml_priority/1000)], User=4, Admin=5); Admin always outranks the others. The admin policy directory is ignored entirely if it isn't root-owned and non-group/other-writable — Mimir must write it with those exact permissions. Antigravity CLI itself (Go-based, closed-source, binary reportedly named 'agy') is a plausible future catalog candidate but its install paths and any admin/MDM mechanism are not yet confirmed from an official source — antigravity.google was unreachable this review; see PR 'Candidates for supported' and 'Unverified'.

CHANGED since last review: a genuine on-device mechanism now exists (GA 2026-07-01, extended to CLI/VS Code 2026-07-08) making this a strong candidate for 'supported'. Two device-level channels, both read by Copilot CLI: (1) native MDM managed preferences for the com.github.copilot domain (macOS profile, string values only with dot-separated nested keys and JSON-encoded arrays/objects; Windows equivalent HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\GitHubCopilot); (2) file-based deployment at /Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json on macOS (/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json on Linux, no native MDM on Linux) - file must be owned by root, not group/world-writable, no symlinks; client restart required to reload. Precedence: MDM-managed > server-managed (org's copilot/managed-settings.json in .github-private, legacy path .github/copilot/settings.json) > file-based > user's own ~/.copilot/config.json — EXCEPT sandbox and permissions.deny/ask/allow, which vendor docs say are composed in the most restrictive direction across delivery methods regardless of this precedence. Keys, re-confirmed directly from github/docs source this review: allowedMcpServers is vendor-documented, verbatim, as intersect ('a server must be permitted by every source to run'); permissions.allow is likewise documented as intersect, not union — same non-obvious stricter-than-expected pattern; deniedMcpServers and permissions.deny/ask are union, deny always wins; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is a string enum ('disable'/'unmanaged'), not a boolean, but still anyTrue-shaped (any source setting 'disable' wins); model (string, top-level key now supersedes legacy permissions.model, last/highest-precedence layer wins); enabledPlugins (union); extraKnownMarketplaces/strictKnownMarketplaces (most-restrictive wins). permissions.limitTo (CLI 1.0.93, 2026-10-07) — a network-domain allowlist ('enforce managed domain boundaries for network requests'; only Domain(...) entries valid, an empty list denies all) that sits alongside permissions.allow/deny/ask with deny still winning — same restriction-allowlist family as allowedMcpServers, so intersect. CONFIRMED this review (direct raw fetch of changelog.md, versions through 1.0.98 / 2026-10-14): 1.0.94 (2026-10-08) confirms a real 'Assisted Permissions' control exists — 'managed policy can disable Assisted Permissions and keep sessions in Manual Approval mode' — but its exact JSON key name is still not pinned down with a quote, so no mergeRule is added yet; 1.0.97 (2026-10-13) confirms managed permission rules show read-only in /config 'unless set by your organization', consistent with the existing permissions.allow/deny/ask model. Carried-forward open research items (key names not yet pinned to an exact quote): autoTier, remoteControl, a richer telemetry object, features.computerUse, an {"overridable": value} wrapper, and the exact 'Assisted Permissions' key name. Caveat still open: GitHub issue github/copilot-cli#4959 (managed 'model' key not reliably applied in non-interactive CLI runs / Copilot desktop app) RE-CONFIRMED OPEN this review via a direct fetch of the issue (latest comment 2026-10-01, reproduced on desktop app v1.1.25) — changelog.md shows no fix in any version through 1.0.98 (2026-10-14) — this still blocks promoting to 'supported'. Recommend promoting to supported once that bug is fixed, or shipping the file-based /Library/Application Support/GitHubCopilot/managed-settings.json output now with a note about the interactive-only model-key caveat. UPDATED this review (direct fetch of changelog.md, versions through 1.0.103 / 2026-10-22): 1.0.102 (2026-10-21) adds an entry reading 'Prompt mode (-p and piped stdin) honors managed Auto model selection', which appears to fix the non-interactive-CLI half of the #4959 bug specifically; a direct re-fetch of #4959 shows it is still OPEN with no linked fix PR, and its most recent comment (Oct 1) reports the bug reproduced on the separate Copilot desktop app (v1.1.25), which this changelog entry doesn't address. So: CLI prompt-mode model routing looks fixed, desktop-app model routing is still unconfirmed/unfixed — still blocking full promotion to 'supported' pending a desktop-side fix or confirmation. 1.0.101 also added assistedApprovalInstructions (a free-text prompt/instruction setting for Assisted Permissions, not a restriction value with a clear direction — not added to mergeRules). The exact 'Assisted Permissions' managed-settings key name is still not pinned down with a quote.

RESOLVED this review: an English-language primary source now corroborates what was previously sourced only from a French-locale page (kiro.dev itself still unreachable for a direct raw fetch — blocked by this session's network policy, consistent every review so far; this is WebSearch-quoted text agreeing across two independent research passes) — admins place a JSON policy file at the OS-protected path, exactly /Library/Application Support/Kiro/managed-settings.json on macOS (requires sudo to create), applying to 'every Kiro surface on the machine, because the IDE and the CLI read the same file,' with a restart required to reload. Schema: a rules array of {capability, effect} objects. Documented rule semantics: the admin layer can only set deny/ask (never allow); deny > ask > allow regardless of scope ('there is no precedence between scopes, the most restrictive effect wins'); headless/non-interactive runs treat every ask as a deny; an invalid policy file (bad JSON, an 'allow' effect from an admin source, or an unrecognized field) fails closed, denying all tools rather than granting unrestricted access — a good match for Mimir's restrictive-wins default. The same managed-settings file also reportedly carries a sign-in-method rule (always deny effect) plus IAM Identity Center details. RESOLVED FURTHER this review (WebSearch, again cross-referencing the official kiro.dev FR-locale mirror): the rule object's fields are capability (required) and effect (required), plus optional match and exclude — the English-page table was cut off in search results and still needs a direct fetch to triple-check wording, but the FR mirror gives the same 4 names. Documented capability values: fs_read, fs_write, shell, web_fetch, web_search, mcp, subagent, skill, power, context, diagnostics, sandbox_network, plus meta-capabilities all/builtin/filesystem. User-level policy lives at ~/.kiro/settings/permissions.yaml (deny/ask/allow, same rules/capability/match/effect shape but YAML), alongside the existing per-user CLI settings at ~/.kiro/settings/cli.json. Kiro CLI remains AWS's rebrand of Amazon Q Developer CLI; the exact rebrand date is still unconfirmed from a primary source. This is a strong 'supported' candidate — the rules-array field names are now reasonably well corroborated, though still not direct-fetch-confirmed on the English page — but /Library/Application Support/Kiro/ is not yet in Mimir's compiled-in path allowlist, so no output is added here — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'.

Terminal coding agent from Factory AI; installed via install script, Homebrew cask (droid) or npm. CONFIRMED (WebSearch snippets, docs.factory.ai still blocked for a direct fetch — blocked by this session's network policy, consistent every review so far): a key named maxAutonomyLevel is an org-level hard cap that clamps the user's own autonomyLevel even if the user sets it higher (limit/kill-switch style), and command allow/deny lists 'accumulate across levels' rather than override. This still reads as org/cloud-distributed configuration (synced from a cloud endpoint), not a macOS-device/MDM-dropped local file — still not a 'supported' candidate. CONFIRMED this review (WebSearch snippets of docs.factory.ai/enterprise/hierarchical-settings-and-org-control, still blocked for a direct fetch): two new org-level kill-switch-shaped keys, cloudSessionSync (boolean, default true, controls cloud session mirroring) and wikiCloudSync (boolean; disabling it blocks AutoWiki endpoints and skips cloud/GitHub wiki sync) — both would be anyFalse if modeled. PARTIALLY RESOLVED this review: a dedicated WebSearch for the disputed local-file lead (/Library/Application Support/Factory/settings.json) and the permissionRules vs. commandAllowlist/commandDenylist naming conflict found no result mentioning a local macOS file at all, and found commandAllowlist/commandDenylist (not permissionRules) as the org-schema names for shell-command allow/deny lists — leaning the conclusion back toward 'cloud-distributed only, no local device file,' though this is still WebSearch snippets, not a direct fetch, so NOT promoted to a confirmed fact; the local-file lead is not retracted outright, just unsupported by this pass. Needs a direct fetch of docs.factory.ai to fully resolve — see PR 'Unverified'.

CONFIRMED this review via WebSearch-quoted text from https://ampcode.com/news/enterprise-managed-settings and https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/settings (ampcode.com itself is still unreachable for a direct fetch): amp.mcpServers is a grant list (union); amp.mcpPermissions is a first-match-wins ordered rule list matching MCP servers by url (remote) or command/args (local), defaulting to allow when nothing matches — a restriction mechanism where rule order matters, so a straight union is not quite right; amp.permissions is a similar first-match-wins rule list for Bash command patterns. Precise managed-settings-vs-workspace precedence is still only strongly implied ('override any other setting'), not stated as an explicit ordered list — recommend one more direct-fetch pass to pin that down before adding mergeRules. Open-source terminal coding agent (TUI) from Charm; installed via Homebrew (charmbracelet/tap/crush) or npm (@charmland/crush). CORRECTED this review (confirmed via a direct fetch of the repo README): crush.json is now explicitly called legacy/deprecated; the primary config is crushrc, a Bash script with Crush-specific builtins (provider add, model add, permissions allow, mcp add), loaded in priority ./.crushrc > ./crushrc > ~/.config/crush/crushrc. crush.json (schema at charm.land/crush.json) still works but is secondary. Both crushrc and crush.json run as trusted code at load time (crushrc is full shell; $(...) in crush.json executes) — relevant to how much Mimir should trust a project-local config file. No enterprise/MDM mechanism documented — individual-developer tool as of this review.

Open-source terminal coding agent CLI from the Qwen team, forked from Gemini CLI and optimized for Qwen3-Coder models; codebase search/edit, shell execution and MCP support. Installed via npm (@qwen-code/qwen-code) or Homebrew (qwen-code). CORRECTED this review: the predicted inheritance from Gemini CLI has arrived — WebSearch-quoted text from the repo's docs/users/configuration/settings.md (not a direct fetch) describes a system settings file that 'takes precedence over user and project settings for all users,' mirroring Gemini CLI's mechanism at /Library/Application Support/QwenCode/settings.json (system overrides) and system-defaults.json (defaults), with env-var overrides QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH/QWEN_CODE_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS_PATH — this specific file path is still WebSearch-sourced, not fetch-confirmed. CONFIRMED this review (direct fetch of github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/issues/13513): that issue, open as of this review, documents the env-var override is honored with no file-ownership check — unlike Gemini CLI's admin policy dir, which is ignored unless root-owned — so a non-admin user can point the CLI at a system-settings file they own and claim system-settings authority (e.g. to redirect model.baseUrl); a maintainer triage comment downgraded it to P3 (arguing the threat model is weak outside a filtered-environment launcher). UPDATED this review (direct fetch of PR #13628, still open, not merged): the fix adds a real ownership/path-containment check — on Unix, the env-var override is honored only if it is a regular file owned by uid 0 (checked with lstat so symlinks aren't followed); on Windows, the resolved path must be inside C:\ProgramData\qwen-code\; otherwise the CLI falls back to the platform default with a one-shot warning. However, the qwen-code review bot's Oct 11/16/19 2026 reviews raised still-open correctness concerns with the fix itself: a Windows UNC path containing '..' segments can pass the containment check, a rejected override falls back silently (which could leave an operator's confinement policy unenforced without any signal), and the change would break existing test fixtures that rely on temp-file overrides. Given the fix is both unmerged and still disputed, this remains a weaker 'supported' candidate than gemini-cli right now; exact policy key names beyond the settings/system-defaults split are still not confirmed with a quote, so no outputs/mergeRules are added — recommend re-checking once #13628 (or a corrected version of it) merges.

RESOLVED this review (direct fetch of 26-config-reference.md, the field-reference doc last review couldn't pin down): exact macOS deployment paths are now confirmed — requirements.toml is read from $GROK_HOME/requirements.toml (a signed cache; default $GROK_HOME is ~/.grok) and /etc/grok/requirements.toml, plus a macOS MDM preference domain ai.x.grok (not a file path); managed_config.toml is read from /etc/grok/managed_config.toml and $GROK_HOME/managed_config.toml (so ~/.grok/managed_config.toml by default). /etc/grok/ is NOT yet in Mimir's compiled-in path allowlist (only /etc/codex/ is) — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'; this remains a 'planned' entry with no outputs. mcp_servers schema confirmed: each server is [mcp_servers.<name>] with command/args/url/type/cwd/enabled/env/headers/bearer_token_env_var/bearer_token_file/oauth*/setup/startup_timeout_sec/tool_timeout_sec/tool_timeouts/expose_image_base64; a separate top-level disabled_mcp_servers list skips servers by name without deleting them. [permission] confirmed as permission.allow/permission.ask/permission.deny (string[] of compact rules like 'Bash(git *)') plus a verbose permission.rules table array, with 'Deny beats ask beats allow' stated explicitly — matching the restriction-allowlist/deny-list family already modeled for Codex. A real 'supported' candidate now that paths and key names are confirmed, pending only the Mimir path-allowlist change — see PR 'Candidates for supported'. Terminal-based AI coding agent from xAI (SpaceXAI), confirmed via two direct raw fetches of the official repo (README and crates/codegen/xai-grok-pager/docs/user-guide/05-configuration.md): a full-screen TUI that edits files, executes shell commands, searches the web and manages long-running tasks; can also run headlessly or embed via the Agent Client Protocol. The repo 'is synced periodically from the SpaceXAI monorepo' and does not accept external contributions. Has a genuine admin-configuration mechanism closely analogous to Codex's: confirmed precedence (highest first) is CLI flags > env vars > requirements.toml/MDM (org-enforced, 'clamps every config layer below') > GROK_CONFIG/GROK_CONFIG_PATH overlay > config.toml (~/.grok/config.toml) > managed_config.toml (org-deployed defaults, overridable) > built-in defaults; requirements.toml telemetry pins ([telemetry] otel_* keys) 'pin over process env' where managed_config.toml does not.

New entry. 'CoCo' — Snowflake's terminal coding agent (CoCo CLI) and companion CoCo Desktop app, requiring a paid Snowflake account or a dedicated CLI trial. Installed via a curl-piped install script (macOS/Linux) or a PowerShell one-liner (Windows); authentication reuses the Snowflake CLI's own connection file, ~/.snowflake/connections.toml. docs.snowflake.com itself was unreachable for a direct raw fetch this review — everything below is WebSearch-quoted from the official managed-settings doc page, not fetch-confirmed. A genuine device-level mechanism is described: managed-settings.json at /Library/Application Support/Cortex/ on macOS (/etc/cortex/ on Linux/WSL, %ProgramData%\Cortex\ on Windows), read by both CoCo CLI and CoCo Desktop; absent the file, the CLI runs unmanaged; if the JSON is invalid or fails schema validation, the CLI fails closed to a restrictive configuration ('Enforcement config error - restricted mode') rather than granting unrestricted access; the file needs admin/root rights to write, so user config/env vars/flags generally can't override it. DOWNGRADED this review: the previously-stated schema (top-level version '1.0'; permissions with tool/skill/MCP-server/account allow/deny lists, pattern example bash(git:*)) is NOT actually quoted verbatim anywhere found this pass. Instead, search turned up two inconsistent schemas across Snowflake's own pages: the managed-settings page references permissions/dangerouslyAllowAll/defaultMode; a separate CLI-settings page describes a different permissions.json with onlyAllow/defaultMode/dangerouslyAllowAll and no allow/deny arrays; a sandbox doc shows permissions.allow/permissions.deny arrays with patterns like Bash(command)/Edit(path)/Read(path)/WebFetch(domain:example.com) — no git-specific example anywhere. A third-party issue (dyoshikawa/rulesync#3012) independently flags the same inconsistency. Given this, the mechanism and path are still credible but the exact schema is now treated as genuinely unsettled rather than just unconfirmed — do not rely on the specific key names above without a direct fetch. A real 'supported' candidate once a direct fetch resolves which schema actually governs managed-settings.json — see PR 'Candidates for supported' and 'Unverified'. No mergeRules or outputs added, and /Library/Application Support/Cortex/ is not yet in Mimir's compiled-in path allowlist — see PR 'Needs Mimir change'.
